world: Photoreal open-world western video game. The third-person camera is locked just behind and slightly above the player the whole time, never cutting, never turning to face him. The player is Tex Lexington, a Black Ethiopian-Texan cowboy in his thirties riding a grey horse: weathered tan cowboy hat, white cotton Ethiopian shamma cloak with a red tibeb border over a brown leather duster, denim, boots with spurs, a revolver on his hip, a lasso on the saddle. Ethiopia on Mars: a frontier town on the rust-red Martian desert under a pink sky with two small moons, red mesas like West Texas, wooden saloon fronts and a windmill beside round stone tukul houses, tall carved Aksum stelae, glass greenhouse domes. Black Ethiopian settlers in white cotton, donkeys with yellow water jerrycans. A towering Martian dust storm on the horizon. Golden low sun.
beats: Tex Lexington canters down the main street of the Mars frontier town; settlers in white cotton look up; a donkey carrying yellow jerrycans crosses in front of him.
The towering Martian dust storm rolls into town, swallowing the mesas, the saloons and the stelae; red dust swirls around Tex and his horse.
Red dust fills the entire frame; only Tex's white shamma cloak and his hat show through the storm.

The storm blows past behind him and the dust clears: the frontier town has become a gleaming future city of Ethiopia on Mars, with copper towers carved like rock-hewn churches, green fields under glass domes, water channels and a train on tall pylons.
Tex rides on through a wide plaza of the future city; Black Ethiopian settlers in white cotton and silver suits wave to him; drones carry water overhead.
Under the two moons Tex slows his horse in front of a church carved into the red rock in the shape of a cross, glowing at dusk, the camera locked behind him.
